pipelines.layout: Layout: <type>/<compiler>/<provider>/, where provider is github, gitlab or azure_dev_ops, e.g. remote/vite/github/workflows/release.yml. A folder <type>/<compiler>/<templateSlug>/<provider>/ wins for that template only. On GitHub the folder becomes .github/ and replaces the workflows of the template; on GitLab and Azure DevOps .gitlab-ci.yml and azure-pipelines.yml replace the ones at the root. A template the repository has no folder for keeps the pipeline it ships with: the official templates are not used as a fallback.

questions.explain_build: Why did build {{runId}} (ref {{ref}}) of microfrontend {{name}} (id {{microfrontendId}}) fail? Read the logs of the failed jobs, explain the cause and suggest a fix.
questions.analyze_deployments: Compare the latest deployment of environment {{environment}} (id {{environmentId}}) with the previous one: which versions and variables changed, and is there anything to check?
questions.explain_dependencies: Analyze the shared dependencies and misaligned peer dependencies across the microfrontends: which conflicts are risky and which should I tackle first?
questions.check_variables: Compare the environment variables across the project's environments: are any defined in one environment and missing from another, production in particular?

usage.hint: Tokens used for this answer, every model step summed. Tokens read from the cache cost far less.

effort.label: Reasoning effort
effort.hint: More effort means deeper reasoning, slower answers and more tokens.

jobs.usage_hint: Tokens used by the agent, every model step summed. One agent works on all the repositories of the job, so the cost belongs to the job. Tokens read from the cache cost far less.
jobs.apply_all_description_one: The proposal is pushed straight onto the base branch of its repository, with all its proposed files and no review. Its CI starts right away, with the repository secrets: review the diff first.
jobs.apply_all_description_other: Each of the {{count}} proposals is pushed straight onto the base branch of its repository, with all its proposed files and no review. Their CI starts right away, with the repository secrets: review the diffs first.
jobs.apply_all_success: Proposals applied onto their base branches
jobs.follow_up_placeholder: Ask the agent for a change, or ask it a question…
jobs.follow_up_running: Wait for the agent to finish to ask for more…
jobs.follow_up_failed: This job failed: start a new job to try again.

new.title: New AI job
new.description: One agent works on the chosen microfrontends together, so a change can span them, such as a shared component and the microfrontends that use it. It proposes the edits for review: nothing is pushed until you apply them.
new.all_hint: Every microfrontend with a linked repository, at most {{max}}.
new.no_repositories: No microfrontend of this project has a linked code repository.
new.prompt_placeholder: e.g. Rename the getUser API of the shell and update the microfrontends that call it
